capture.final_message:
Treat neighborhoods of \(0\) through the submodule basis supplied by a linear topology.

- The first conjunct is exactly the standard characterization of `IsLinearTopology`: the neighborhoods of \(0\) have a basis consisting of submodules that themselves are neighborhoods.
- For the second, test convergence against a basic neighborhood \(N\) of \(0\). From \(b \to 0\), eventually \(b_i \in N\). Since \(R\) is viewed as a left module over itself, \(N\) is closed under multiplication on the left, so \(a_i b_i \in N\) for every such \(i\), regardless of how \(a_i\) varies.
- Thus \(a_i b_i\) is eventually in every neighborhood of \(0\), which is precisely \(a b \to 0\).

The essential mechanism is absorption by open left submodules; no convergence or boundedness assumption on \(a\) is needed.
